holidays.name: National Grape Popsicle Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the frozen purple treat that stains tongues, lips, and the occasional white T-shirt. Break out a grape popsicle and let your tongue turn a suspicious shade of violet.
holidays.origin: Like many food holidays, it is an unofficial observance that grew out of popular culture and social media food-day calendars. It has no known single founder or official proclamation.
holidays.funFact: The popsicle was reportedly invented by accident in 1905 when 11-year-old Frank Epperson left a cup of soda powder and water with a stirring stick outside on a cold night in San Francisco.

holidays.name: Sun Screen Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to slathering on SPF before the summer sun gets going. It is a reminder that a sunburn is a terrible souvenir.
holidays.origin: Observed in late May as the unofficial start of summer approaches in the Northern Hemisphere, it is promoted as a seasonal skin-health reminder. Its exact origin is unclear.
holidays.funFact: Sunscreen was popularized after chemist Benjamin Green developed an early version during World War II to protect soldiers. His red petrolatum formula was sticky and smelled awful, and it later inspired Coppertone.

holidays.name: Cellophane Tape Day
holidays.description: A salute to clear sticky tape, which fixes torn pages, wraps presents badly, and hides in plain sight whenever you need it. Celebrate by finding the end of the roll on your first try, if you can.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance honoring the invention of cellophane tape. 3M engineer Richard Drew developed Scotch tape in the 1930s.
holidays.funFact: The 'Scotch' name came from an auto body painter who complained that an early masking tape prototype was stingy with its adhesive. He told Drew to take it back to his 'Scotch' bosses, and the name stuck.

holidays.name: Sleepy Head Day
holidays.description: A cozy, slightly ridiculous holiday that encourages everyone to sleep in, hit snooze, and wake up when they feel like it. Pajamas are the official dress code.
holidays.origin: Sleepy Head Day is traditionally linked to Finland, where it is celebrated on July 27. It is sometimes confused with other sleepy observances, and the Finnish tradition involves dunking the last person awake into water. Treat this one as a playful, loosely observed nap-themed excuse.
holidays.funFact: In the Finnish tradition, called Unikeonpäivä, the last person in the household to wake up is traditionally thrown into a lake or bucket of water.
